paras: The Sixth Street mob beating was an attack on a Black man by a crowd of white bystanders on Sixth Street in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on the night of 2 October 1903. After a stabbing in a saloon, a crowd chased three Black men and beat the one it caught while a policeman held him, until he was found to be "the wrong man" and released. The Minneapolis Journal called the affair a "miniature race war" that police interference kept from becoming a lynching.

According to the Journal, at about 10 o'clock one of three Black men in a saloon on Sixth Street between Hennepin and Nicollet avenues stabbed a white man in the neck "after an altercation" that the paper did not describe. The white man was reported not seriously wounded.

The three men ran from the saloon, pursued by "a small crowd which grew rapidly." The crowd surrounded two of them while the third disappeared down the street with a knife in his hand; of the two, one was captured and the other got away.

While a policeman held the captured man, "excited bystanders" repeatedly struck him over the head, one with a closed knife, until blood spurted from his scalp. It was then found that he was the wrong man, and he was allowed to go, in the paper's words "much the worse for rough handling."
The Journal reported no arrest of the man who did the stabbing or of anyone who beat the captured man, and no later report on the case was found.

The only report found is a short local item on page 6 of the Minneapolis Journal of 3 October 1903, headed "SLUGGED A HELPLESS MAN" with the subhead "Pinioned by a Policeman, a Negro Is Pounded by Excited Bystanders." The headline and the "wrong man" detail drew attention to the beating of a held prisoner, while the item gave the stabbing accusation without attribution and described the clash as a "miniature race war." No coverage of the incident was found in other white papers or in the Black press.

accounts.label: Minneapolis Journal local report
accounts.gist: After a saloon stabbing, a growing crowd chased three Black men and beat a captured one held by a policeman until police intervention stopped what threatened to be a lynching; he proved to be the wrong man.

framing.detail: Headline "SLUGGED A HELPLESS MAN" and "wrong man" stress the victim's helplessness, but the report presents the stabbing accusation as fact and calls the affair a "miniature race war."

quotes: A miniature race war raged on Sixth street between Hennepin and Nicollet avenues last night and only the interference of the police prevented an affair which promised a lynching.
While the captured man was held by a policeman, he was repeatedly struck over the head by the excited bystanders, one of whom used a closed knife until the blood spurted from the wounded scalp.
About this time it was found that he was the wrong man and he was allowed to go, much the worse for rough handling.
